rubric.task: My response directly addresses the prompt and uses the specified source.
rubric.language: My sentences use the target grammar and have readable punctuation.
rubric.physics: I checked values, units, and the difference between source evidence and prediction.
rubric.clarity: My ideas are in a clear order and a classmate could understand them.

A2.01.title: Introduce yourself to a physics study group
A2.01.prompt: Write a short introduction with your name (or an invented name), academic interests, the classes you take, your typical study routine, and one polite question for a classmate.
A2.01.languageReminder: Use present simple correctly; include a greeting; ask one clear question.
A2.01.physicsReminder: Do not include real personal details unless you wish to.

A2.01.title: Ask about a class schedule
A2.01.prompt: Write a polite email to a fictional course assistant to confirm the location and start time of Thursday's laboratory introduction. Use the welcome-session notice in reading R3.
A2.01.languageReminder: Include a subject line, Dear..., two clear questions, and an appropriate closing.
A2.01.physicsReminder: Mention 2:00 p.m. and Lab 3 as the details you are checking, rather than inventing a different schedule.

A2.02.title: Describe a set of quantities
A2.02.prompt: Describe the sample values in reading R1 using four short sentences. Include at least a length, a mass, a time interval, and a voltage.
A2.02.languageReminder: Write a space between each value and SI unit symbol; use correct unit names and plural forms.
A2.02.physicsReminder: The values in R1 are illustrative, not results from a real experiment.

A2.02.title: Explain equipment and measurements
A2.02.prompt: Write a paragraph about Nora's desk in reading R2. Explain how many instruments she has and which measurements she records.
A2.02.languageReminder: Use there is/there are, some equipment, how many or how much, and at least two numerical values with units.
A2.02.physicsReminder: Separate instrument count from measurement count.

A2.03.title: Describe the arrangement of equipment
A2.03.prompt: Using reading R1 or the virtual equipment scene, describe where at least four items are located in relation to one another.
A2.03.languageReminder: Use there is/are, next to, on, under, between, or to the left/right of; give a clear reference direction.
A2.03.physicsReminder: Describe only positions supported by the reading or scene.

A2.03.title: Guide a new student
A2.03.prompt: Write numbered instructions that help a classmate identify items in a fictional teaching-room layout, without handling powered apparatus.
A2.03.languageReminder: Use first, next, then and finally; write three to five short imperative sentences.
A2.03.physicsReminder: Do not turn these language exercises into real equipment operating instructions.

A2.04.title: Describe motion shown by a model
A2.04.prompt: Describe a simulated moving cart from a provided source in your reading library. State what it is doing now and how it usually moves in the example.
A2.04.languageReminder: Use present simple and present continuous in distinct sentences.
A2.04.physicsReminder: Avoid claiming an exact speed unless the source provides it.

A2.04.title: Describe two classroom activities
A2.04.prompt: Write about a routine in a physics class and a different activity happening now. An invented teaching example is acceptable if clearly described as fictional.
A2.04.languageReminder: Use adverbs such as usually and now, plus two verbs describing change.
A2.04.physicsReminder: Keep the time references consistent with your verb forms.

A2.05.title: Compare two cable lengths
A2.05.prompt: In a fictional virtual model, Cable X is 60 cm long and Cable Y is 80 cm long. Compare their lengths and explain which cable is longer.
A2.05.languageReminder: Use longer than, shorter than, as ... as (where relevant), and correct cm formatting.
A2.05.physicsReminder: Do not use the word more accurate unless you have a valid accuracy reference.

A2.05.title: Write a measurement comparison
A2.05.prompt: Choose two values from one A2.05 reading source. Write a short paragraph comparing the quantities and identifying their units.
A2.05.languageReminder: Use one comparative and one complete sentence explaining a difference.
A2.05.physicsReminder: Do not compare different physical quantities as though they had the same unit.

A2.06.title: Rewrite fictional room rules
A2.06.prompt: Write a short, clear notice for a fictional teaching room. Include an obligation, a prohibition, and a recommendation.
A2.06.languageReminder: Use must/have to, must not, and should correctly.
A2.06.physicsReminder: This exercise does not replace real instructor-led laboratory safety policies.

A2.06.title: Ask for clarification
A2.06.prompt: Write a brief conversation between a student and an instructor about a confusing instruction in a virtual lab.
A2.06.languageReminder: Use Can I...?, Could you repeat...?, and a clear response.
A2.06.physicsReminder: Do not suggest proceeding with an uncertain or potentially dangerous real-life procedure.

A2.07.title: Report a completed virtual experiment
A2.07.prompt: Using one supplied reading source, describe four steps that took place in the completed fictional experiment.
A2.07.languageReminder: Use simple past forms, including at least one regular and one irregular verb.
A2.07.physicsReminder: Report actions from the source, not imaginary laboratory results.

A2.07.title: Summarize an observation
A2.07.prompt: Write a short paragraph about what was recorded and what was observed during the fictional experiment.
A2.07.languageReminder: Use yesterday, then, and finally where appropriate; separate process from observation.
A2.07.physicsReminder: Do not describe the observation as a proven physical explanation.

A2.08.title: Explain an interruption
A2.08.prompt: Write four sentences about a fictional student working on a virtual experiment when the display suddenly stopped responding.
A2.08.languageReminder: Use was/were + -ing and one completed simple-past event with when or while.
A2.08.physicsReminder: Distinguish the interruption from an unverified explanation of its cause.

A2.08.title: Request technical help
A2.08.prompt: Write a polite message describing a virtual lab issue, when it happened, and what was happening at the time.
A2.08.languageReminder: Use an accurate past time reference and a request for clarification or help.
A2.08.physicsReminder: Do not prescribe real electrical troubleshooting procedures.

A2.09.title: Write a progress update
A2.09.prompt: Write a short message to a fictional project partner saying what you have already completed and what you have not finished yet.
A2.09.languageReminder: Use have/has + past participle with already and yet.
A2.09.physicsReminder: Make it clear that these are fictional course tasks rather than real results.

A2.09.title: Compare past and recent work
A2.09.prompt: Write about one activity completed at a specific past time and another activity completed recently.
A2.09.languageReminder: Use simple past with a finished time and present perfect when the exact finished time is unimportant.

A2.10.title: Explain a simple cause and effect
A2.10.prompt: Using the assumptions in a supplied source, explain one simple cause-and-effect relationship in a virtual physics model.
A2.10.languageReminder: Use because and so in two separate sentences.
A2.10.physicsReminder: State the model's conditions explicitly and distinguish model behavior from measurement.

A2.10.title: Make a conditional prediction
A2.10.prompt: Write three short conditional statements about simple physics situations provided in the reading.
A2.10.languageReminder: Use if + present simple and a clearly formed result clause.
A2.10.physicsReminder: Do not assert predictions outside the source assumptions.

A2.11.title: Describe the simulated graph
A2.11.prompt: Use the displayed virtual cart graph or its accessible data table. Describe the horizontal axis, vertical axis, and increasing trend from 0 s to 4 s.
A2.11.languageReminder: Include the labels Time (s) and Position (m), and use increased from ... to ... correctly.
A2.11.physicsReminder: The graph uses simulated numbers; do not call them measured values.

A2.11.title: Predict carefully
A2.11.prompt: Describe the trend in one source graph, then write a cautious sentence about what might happen next.
A2.11.languageReminder: Use may or might, and clearly identify the prediction.
A2.11.physicsReminder: Do not present an extrapolation as an observed data point.

A2.12.title: Integrated virtual-lab mini report
A2.12.prompt: Write a short report about the virtual cart model using the graph and data table. Include a title, source, process, observations and a cautious conclusion.
A2.12.languageReminder: Include numerical values and units, sequence words, past-tense or present-tense descriptions consistently, and one clear limitation.
A2.12.physicsReminder: Say simulated/model values rather than measured experimental evidence.

A2.12.title: Explain the result to a classmate
A2.12.prompt: Write a friendly explanation for a classmate of what the virtual-cart graph shows and what it does not prove.
A2.12.languageReminder: Use simple graph language and a comparison or cause-and-effect sentence supported by the source.
A2.12.physicsReminder: Clearly separate an observation, a model assumption and a prediction.
